description.narrative: Butalejja district is one of the eight (08) districts located in the Mt. Elgon region in Uganda. The districts comprise of three altitude zones namely; Low, Mid and Highland altitudes. The Elgon region districts are continuously facing reoccurrence of landslides,mud slides and flash flooding that are becoming more frequent and severe with climatic changes. Given the geographical formation ofBulambuli and Butalejja district, the high altitude is a hot spot for mudslides and landslides. The mid altitude has moderate but more indirect experiences, and the low altitude is highly prone to flash floods. The occurrence of these disasters affects people’s lives, livelihoods, property, crops, environmental degradation, destruction of infrastructures (roads, schools, health centers etc.),pollution and contamination of existing water sources as well as destruction of other WASH infrastructures. These consequently presents a serious public health risk as communities continued to fetch water from un safe sources, have no access to latrine thus creating economic disruption, food insecurity, disease outbreak and in the extremes death of humans, animals and poultry. On 3rd April, 2024, A heavy down pour was experienced in the Elgon region which resulted in to a massive flash floods, landslides and mudslides in the region affecting mostly Butalejja district (Himutu sub county, Mazimasa sub county, Kachonga sub county, Butaleja Sub- County and Butaleja Town Council) in Butaleja District as the mostly affected district, Bulambuli district has as well been affected by the disaster. The floods were characterized by heavy downpour coupled with overflowing of rivers from the Elgon region into Butaleja and Bulambuli leading to destruction of people’s houses, crops, animals,water sources, sanitation facilities and community infrastructure such as roads, health facilities. According to the Uganda National Meteorological Authority (UNMA), weather outlook for the 3rd dekad of April 2024, the region will be among the areas withthe highest peak of rainfall which will be above the normal trend thus this will still create high chances of increased flooding and landslide in the Mt Elgon sub region which is a major risk factor for landslide occurrence. Currently most of the areas in the High-altitude zones are soggy with water oozing from the ground at different points. This is an indicator of the increased risk of landslides in these areas. According to the joint assessment conducted by Uganda Red Cross Society (URCS), other partners and stakeholders from Butalejja district local government, a total of 5,102 households and 25,510 population (12,245M, F13,265) were severely affected in Butalejja district following the recent flash flood in the districtwith one (01) death registeredwith an anticipation of more death to be registered following the number of injuries. The most affected populations are from Himutu sub county, Mazimasa sub county, Kachonga sub county, Butaleja Sub- County and Butaleja Town Council)in Butaleja District.The floods impact resulted in to displacement of families majority of which are women and children affected, destruction of infrastructures (roads, schools, health centers etc.), pollution and contamination of existing water sources as well as destructionof other WASH infrastructures such as sanitation facilities at both household and institutional level in Bulambuli and Butalejja district. Apparently, access to safe water remained hindered as most of the water supply infrastructures such as existinggravity flow schemes with public water tap stands, springs and boreholes as main safe water sources have been affected with the flooding impact leading to access to unsafe water for drinking and other domestic use from unprotected and open water sources whichare deemed to be contaminated, With collapsed sanitation facilities both at institutional and household level and poor waste management resulting from the flooding, contamination of ground water is anticipated to be higher due to continued seepage, MoistLow lying areas are not suitable for sinking latrines given the loose nature of soils as well as high water table prevailing risk of open defecation. Unspecified number of household latrines have been buried in mud while others were completely washed away yet water continues to ooze increasing the risk of open water sources, springs and borehole contamination

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
